subject: Add-ons pricing: retention / tracing / dashboards — options and proposed path

Subject: Quick question on add-on pricing (retention, tracing, dashboards)

Hi Laura,

We're evaluating Redwood's observability add-ons as part of our production rollout. Specifically we need pricing and packaging guidance for three items:
- Long-term retention (30/90/365 day buckets) for traces and logs
- Tracing: full span retention vs sampled traces (per-span pricing vs sampling model)
- Advanced dashboards: seat-based vs host-based vs metric/event volume pricing

Two asks: can you share a succinct options sheet (pricing bands + recommended defaults for a mid-market customer with ~120 hosts and a bursty traffic pattern), and confirm whether there are committed-discount paths or pilot credits available for an initial 6-month evaluation?

We're trying to scope costs before our procurement meeting next week. Appreciate a short note or a one-pager.

Thanks,
Nora

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Quick question on add-on pricing (retention, tracing, dashboards)

Hi Nora — great to hear from you and congrats on the rollout. High level answers below; I attached a one-pager and a sample pricing workbook for numbers you can drop your host counts into (redwood_observability_options.pdf, ACME-obs-pricing-20280312.xlsx).

Summary (short):
1) Retention tiers
   - 30-day: metered at $0.02/GB-month (default for dev/staging)
   - 90-day: slab pricing, $0.015/GB-month for first 50TB, $0.012/GB beyond
   - 365-day: commitment required; list $0.009/GB-month with a 12-month commit and minimum monthly commitment
   - Recommendation for you: 90-day default with selective 365-day for critical services (db, auth)

2) Tracing model
   - Full-span retention: priced per-span ingested ($0.0006/span) — good for short-term deep debugging
   - Sampled + transaction index: priced per million sampled transactions ($12 / 1M sampled tx) with retention tier applied to sampled data
   - Recommendation: use sampled model at 10-15% with full-span for key services during incident windows

3) Advanced dashboards
   - Seat-based: $60/user/month for standard dashboards (good for small core teams)
   - Host-based (metrics-backed): $5/host/month for dashboards with unlimited seat viewers; scales better for ops-heavy orgs
   - Volume-based: for very high cardinality metrics, meter by ingested metric-GB; this is rare for your profile

Discounts / commits / pilots
   - Typical mid-market path: 12-month commit -> 10% discount on add-ons. 24-month -> 18%
   - We have a one-time pilot credit program (applies toward add-ons) for new customers: up to $25k credit for a 6-month evaluation, subject to exec approval.

Next steps:
- If you want, I can propose a specific pricing path tailored to your 120 hosts and typical ingest rates.
- Also happy to run a 30-minute alignment call with Marcus (pricing lead) and Aditya (solutions SE) to fast-track concessions.

I've attached the one-pager. If you want numbers in the body I can paste them but thought the workbook would be cleaner.

Best,

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 13 Mar 2028 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Quick question on add-on pricing (AcmeCloud) — request for concession guidance

Team — forwarding Nora's note and the one-pager. AcmeCloud is interested in a 6-month trial ahead of a larger commit. Their profile: ~120 hosts, bursty peaks during business hours, 3 primary services (web, auth, data).

Ask: can we approve a pilot credit up to $25k and an introductory discount path? My initial thought is to offer: 12-month commit = 12% off add-ons (not 10%), plus $15k pilot credit applied to first 3 months of add-on consumption. If they convert to 24m we increase to 20% and roll the remaining credit into month 1 invoice.

Risks: concession erosion on small total contract value if we over-credit. If we can't do 12% straight, I'd accept 10% + $20k credits. Also need to confirm whether we can make the pilot credit conditional (pay-as-you-go until commit) in the SOW.

Can you review and flag any guardrails I should include? Also attaching the pricing workbook with a shaded 'concession' tab.

Thanks — LA

--
Attachment: ACME-obs-pricing-20280312.xlsx
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 11:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Quick question on add-on pricing (AcmeCloud) — request for concession guidance

Laura / Aditya — thanks for the context. I support a path that balances near-term trial friction with preserving ACV economics. My suggestion:

- Offer 10% off add-ons on a 12-month commit (this is our standard mid-market anchor).
- Add a $20k pilot credit (applies to the first 90 days of add-on usage), refundable in the sense that it is consumed against invoices, not a cash refund.
- Include a clause: if they convert to a 24-month commit within 6 months, we apply an additional 8% retrospective credit to add-on spend (equivalent to bumping to 18%).
- Require minimum monthly commit of $5k on add-ons for the 12-month path to avoid tiny deals gaming the credit.

Also recommend we propose a hybrid retention strategy (90-day default + selective 365-day for 6 core services) in the SOW — we price the 365-day bucket at the committed rate and simplify the billing.

If Aditya is good on implementation feasibility, I'm fine for you to send the revised offer to Nora.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Pricing & Packaging
Redwood Inference

Subject: Observability add-ons — proposed commercial path (pilot + commit options)

Hi Nora — following internal alignment, here is a concise commercial path you can take to trial and then commit. I summarised items from the workbook for clarity.

Option A — 12-month commit (recommended pilot path)
  - 10% discount on observability add-ons (retention + tracing + dashboards)
  - $20,000 pilot credit applied to add-on invoices for the first 90 days
  - Minimum monthly add-on commit: $5,000
  - Hybrid retention recommendation: 90-day default, enable 365-day for up to 6 critical services at committed rate

Option B — 24-month commit (better economics)
  - 18% discount on add-ons
  - $10,000 pilot credit available (if still requested)
  - If you convert from Option A to B within 6 months, we'll apply an additional retrospective credit equal to 8% of billed add-on spend (bringing total to 18%)

Technical & billing notes:
  - Tracing: recommend sampled ingestion (10-15%) with full-span capture for incidents. Pricing will reflect sampled plus an emergency full-span ramp cap.
  - Dashboards: seat-based charges can be swapped to host-based for ops-heavy use; we outlined cost comparisons in the workbook.
  - Credits are consumed against invoices (no cash refunds). Pilot credit end date: 90 days from SOW start date.

Next steps: if this looks good I can send a short SOW and DocuSign proposal. Link to proposed DocuSign draft: https://docusign.com/tx/AC-2028-042/proposal

If you'd like a quick call to walk through numbers in the spreadsheet, Marcus and Aditya can join.

Thanks,
